question: With the Gemma layer norms and the q/k head norms routed through the batch- and position-invariant Triton RMSNorm (R152 image over R139), do both profiles become output-identical through c64, stay repeat-exact at 100-300-token prompts, and what does c1 speed do?

evidence_base.census: R151a-e cleared the GDN decode/prefill kernels, paged attention decode/prefill, argmax, the two-card all-reduce, the gated norm, and (R149) the FP16 head; R151f found the vllm ir rms_norm/fused_add_rms_norm kernel non-invariant: a row's bits depend on its slot in the batch (first differing row varies 4-22 by data, permutation fails), while R151g found the Triton rmsnorm_fn invariant and repeat-exact at every M 1-256 on hidden 5120 and head 256 across seeds, and 29-35 us vs 43-66 us for the ir kernel
evidence_base.mechanism: R30 already special-cased two rows for this kernel; R152 generalizes by replacing the kernel rather than the row count

treatment.residual: the fused add stays an exact fp16 add in torch; only the normalization kernel changes
treatment.image: neural-download/vllm-openai-xpu:qwen38-fp8-mtp1-triton-rmsnorm-r152 over R139, built by repro/qwen38-27b-fp8-vllm-tp2-asrock-b70/build-triton-rmsnorm-r152-image.sh; contract opt-in EXPECTED_LAYERNORM_SHA256

run_order: mtp0-a, mtp0-b: same-image MTP0 controls (new oracle, since the norm arithmetic changes c1)
mtp1-a, mtp1-b with the 100-300-token repeat probe on mtp1-b

gates.G4: workload, canaries, cache zero, FP16 verifier marker, R152 markers on both ranks
gates.G6: c1..c64 every output equal to its sequential oracle on both profiles

performance_recording.expectation: the Triton norm is ~30 us faster per call than the ir kernel; ~130 norm calls per step could show as a small c1 gain

on_pass: R152 supersedes R139 as the identity-qualified image: extend the published concurrency claim to c64, present speed for the headline decision, publish the patch and binaries the same way as R139
on_failure: record residual mismatches; remaining un-censused ops are the embedding gather, rotary, and elementwise activations
